context_only: # tp v1.0.1 — tp says what round 1 will read

tasks.title: Export the uncut floor count from internal/engine
tasks.acceptance: internal/engine exports the uncut floor population as a function and internal/cli/ground.go's groundFloorSize calls it instead of duplicating the count, with lines_removed read on every edit. Verified by running on one fixture, a spec carrying cut units and no frontmatter: the exported function equals the line count of `tp ground <spec> --units` while the candidate-inclusive population does not. The closure states why neither engine.FloorUnits nor engine.FloorIndexRows was the answer, their difference being identically zero against real cut counts of 33, 15, 97, 53 and 6 across five specs, and says whether GroundCoverageOf's Emitted now calls the new function or stays separate.

tasks.title: tp lint reports the two floor quantities
tasks.acceptance: `tp lint <spec>` emits floor_size and cut as siblings of structured_elements, with section 6 row 1's test and a cut test both written first and observed red against the unfixed code on one shared fixture, a spec with at least one cut unit and no frontmatter. A third test pins that lint's payload is byte-identical under --compact and --quiet, which is what section 2 claims and what round 2 measured. Section 2's derived by and pinned by cells for both fields are filled in with the real function and test names copied from the tests, and committed as part of this task.

tasks.title: Split resolveRolePanel into resolver plus refusing wrapper
tasks.acceptance: resolveRolePanel becomes a pure resolution function plus a wrapper carrying the refusals and both output.Notice loops, and its two callers, internal/cli/review.go and internal/cli/audit.go, keep the wrapper with stdout, stderr and exit codes diffed identical before and after on the same tree, including the auditors-only refusal path. The task's first act is the decision section 7 asks for, since engine.roleUnits is already a pure resolution serving a read-only consumer: the closure says whether the shared pure half landed in internal/engine beside it or in internal/cli, and why a third copy was avoided. Tests are written red first and their names are then written into section 7, which currently says task 3 names them.

tasks.title: tp lint reports review_panel
tasks.acceptance: `tp lint <spec>` emits review_panel as a JSON list of reviewer role ids equal to those a round-1 `tp review <spec>` emission with no --diff-from carries, obtained through resolver-split's pure function so that lint gains no second derivation. Section 6 row 2 is written first and observed red on its constructed fixture, a temporary corpus in which exactly one role declares domains and a spec whose frontmatter does not match, reproducing the recorded counts of one role at HEAD against two under the mutant. No test asserts parity across this repository's own corpus, because no reviewer role in it declares domains and the filter is therefore inert, which round 2 measured as zero domain-mismatch skips over every spec.

tasks.title: Pin the sibling rule that still reports
tasks.acceptance: A test in internal/engine covers section 6 row 8 on the fixture that separates, a backticked section-and-step reference whose target section holds a numbered list shorter than the step named, giving broken-cross-ref one and vague-language zero at HEAD against broken-cross-ref zero under a mutant that blanks inline spans for every rule, with the mutant built and observed red before the test is accepted. The closure measures orphan-list-item's invariance under the same mutant rather than arguing it, which is the half of row 8's proof round 2 found unmeasured. Rows 4 through 7 close with --covered-by citing 65406160 and each existing test's actual counts, which differ from the rows' fixture counts and are quoted as they are.
source_sections: ## 3. The fence and the inline span

tasks.title: Ship the spec-writing rules to SKILL.md
tasks.acceptance: Every bullet in section 4 except the last, which is precedent, lands in skills/tp/SKILL.md, and the closure gives the count it derived from the bullet list rather than restating a number the spec does not carry. The fenced-command rule as shipped names both the interpreter and the binary, since naming bash alone leaves the binary free and round 2 recorded that gap. For each rule the closure states whether an author can check it while writing or only after a grading round, because a rule judgeable only afterwards costs rounds rather than saving them.

tasks.title: Document the three lint fields for release
tasks.acceptance: README.md documents the three fields tp lint adds, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json's version is bumped before any tag. The release notes state the case the cycle measured, that review_panel replaces an emission with a lint invocation, and cite spec/1.0.1-measurements.md section 11 for the byte counts rather than quoting them. They also say plainly that the release shipped with its review round unconverged at its cap, and why: five grading rounds refuted five successive sets of sentences about code that did not exist yet.

tasks.title: Pin what lint reports where review refuses
tasks.acceptance: When a spec deactivates every reviewer, `tp lint` reports review_panel as an empty JSON list and exits 0 while `tp review` still exits 2, each pinned by a test written first and observed red. Lint emits none of the wrapper's notices, measured as empty stderr on a corpus patched to make review write them, where round 2 measured review at 86 bytes against lint at zero. Section 6 row 3 is written on its fixture, a spec deactivating one role that is actually a reviewer in the corpus, reproducing the recorded counts of one role at HEAD against two under a mutant that ignores the frontmatter override.

tasks.title: REFERENCE.md distinguishes the two floor_size quantities
tasks.acceptance: skills/tp/REFERENCE.md states that lint's floor_size is the live text's floor while the floor_size in tp review's ungrounded envelope is the latest emitted round's frozen index, and gives the condition under which they agree. The paragraph is written after lint's field exists so that both quantities can be run and compared rather than described, and the closure quotes the two numbers it saw diverge on one spec.
